name: Apollo CSM Block II
dispatch: The Command Module was the only piece of Apollo that came home — everything else was spent and thrown away along the route. That made it the part that could not fail on reentry, and reentry from the Moon was the hardest version of the problem: the capsule met the atmosphere at nearly eleven kilometres a second, half again as fast as anything returning from Earth orbit, wrapped in a fireball hot enough to boil steel. Its answer was an ablative heat shield engineered to char and peel away in a controlled way, carrying the heat off with it. Block II was the version that flew crews — the ground-up redesign forced by the Apollo 1 fire — and it brought every astronaut who set out for the Moon back alive.
description: The lunar-capable Command and Service Module that carried Apollo astronauts to lunar orbit between 1968 and 1972. Eleven flights — including Apollo 13’s improvised lifeboat configuration — plus three Skylab visits and the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project.
